# Assessment — #486: Remote-only (client) install: connect to a remote assistant/stack

_Codebase assessment against 0.13.0-beta.3 (2026-07-12). Effort: **M**._

## Current state (already merged)

The overwhelming majority of #486 is already merged at 0.13.0-beta.3. Phase 2 of the runtime-modes plan (the issue's primary implementation phase) is DONE per docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes-plan.md §7/§10 and verified in code: connection management lives at /connections outside /admin in the host app (packages/ui/src/routes/connections/+page.svelte, /connections/new/+page.ts redirect alias, packages/ui/src/routes/api/connections/{+server.ts,[id]/,active/}); the internal model is renamed to "connection" with a `kind` field ('local-opencode' | 'remote-opencode' | 'openpalm-client-api') and read-time defaulting, while endpoints.json under OP_HOME/config keeps its name with a lazy legacy migration (packages/ui/src/lib/server/endpoints.ts:29-83,103-143). The `pwa-static` host mode exists with connection-scoped capabilities and a public /api/runtime (packages/ui/src/lib/server/features.ts:31-137). The client-only artifact shipped as packages/client (adapter-static SPA, no @openpalm/lib — enforced by tests/purity.test.ts): IndexedDB ConnectionStore with kind/locked/isDefault and encrypted secrets (src/lib/connections/index.ts, src/lib/connections/secrets.ts), a full /connections manager with per-connection health probes incl. CORS-blocked disambiguation (src/routes/connections/+page.svelte), a direct browser transport with Basic ('openpalm' default username) / Bearer auth (src/lib/transport/index.ts), and chat with a "via {connection}" indicator plus redirect to /connections/new when no connection is active (src/routes/chat/+page.svelte:231). The wizard deep-link landed in both landing resolvers: pwa-static + 0 connections → /connections/new (packages/client/src/lib/resolve-landing.ts; packages/ui/src/lib/resolve-landing.ts:92-96), and the host resolver also implements the #440 remote-only rule (not_installed + accessible connection → /chat, resolve-landing.ts:84-86). The setup wizard has the "I'll set this up later" no-AI escape hatch explicitly documented as the client-only path (packages/ui/src/routes/setup/steps/Screen1ModelsStep.svelte:248-266). The PWA manifest + service worker (the issue's Phase 6 slice) landed via @vite-pwa/sveltekit with NetworkFirst runtime-config.json and credential-caching exclusions (packages/client/vite.config.ts, tests/pwa-config.test.ts). On the remote-assistant side, Guardian /oc/* ingress with Basic principal auth exists (packages/guardian/src/proxy.ts OC_PREFIX, auth.ts basicTokenAuthStrategy, state-db.ts SQLite principal registry), with an opt-in direct-ingress listener (GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS, port 3830 in packages/skeleton/system/stack/portals.compose.yml:89,114), a CORS allowlist (GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, config.ts:31-52), and an admin API for minting 'direct' principals (admin.ts). The CLI serves the client on stable loopback port 3890 (`openpalm app`, packages/cli/src/commands/app.ts + lib/client-server.ts) and the assistant container co-serves the client on OP_CLIENT_PORT (3810). What does NOT exist: (a) a stack-less entry point — `openpalm app` goes through startUIServer which calls ensureValidState() (packages/cli/src/lib/ui-server.ts:506 → cli-state.ts:23-30) and hard-fails on a machine without `openpalm install`, so "no local stack, UI is the only process" is not actually reachable via the CLI (only `openpalm admin` tolerates not-installed, and it lands on the install wizard); (b) the 'openpalm-client-api' kind is inert — the client add-form hardcodes kind:'remote-opencode' (packages/client/src/routes/connections/+page.svelte:209) and the host addConnection() never persists a kind (endpoints.ts:367-387), with no kind-aware URL/UX for the guardian /oc base path; (c) no user-facing provisioning of remote-client credentials — guardian 'direct' principals are mintable only via POST /admin/principals with the admin token file, and no host-UI/CLI surface or doc-driven flow hands a user a credential to paste into the client (pairing/QR is deferred to #511 per plan §12.3 item 4 and ui-runtime-modes.md "Not Yet Shipped"); (d) requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections is computed but has zero consumers (ui-runtime-modes.md Security Boundaries — Phase 6.5/#557).

## Remaining work

- [ ] Decide and implement the stack-less client entry point: make `openpalm app` (and/or bare `openpalm` in pwa-static mode) serve the host UI + client on a machine with NO local install, mirroring `openpalm admin`'s resolveServeState() tolerance — change the non-admin branch of startUIServer (packages/cli/src/lib/ui-server.ts:506) to use resolveServeState() when openTarget==='client', and skip stack bring-up; landing then falls through to /connections/new via the existing pwa-static resolver. Alternative (document-only): declare the client-only install to be the assistant-container-served client / future hosted PWA (#511) and close this item with docs.
- [ ] Wire or explicitly descope the 'openpalm-client-api' connection kind: either add a kind selector to the client add-connection form (packages/client/src/routes/connections/+page.svelte:209 currently hardcodes 'remote-opencode') and to the host ConnectionInput (packages/ui/src/lib/server/endpoints.ts:367-387 drops kind on add/update), with guardian-aware URL handling (auto-append/validate the /oc base path and probe /oc health), or record the descope in ui-runtime-modes.md and the issue (guardian connections = enter base URL ending in /oc with a Basic principal credential).
- [ ] Provide a minimal remote-credential provisioning path so a client can actually authenticate to a remote stack's guardian: either (preferred, small) a documented manual flow — enable GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS, add the client origin to GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, mint a 'direct' principal via the guardian admin API using op_guardian_admin_token (docs/operations/manual-headless-install.md names the secret) — added to docs/managing-openpalm.md; or a host-UI affordance on /connections that mints a direct principal and shows the id/secret once (full pairing/QR UX stays in #511).
- [ ] Add an end-to-end verification of the remote-attach path: stack e2e (or documented release smoke) where the packages/client transport connects cross-origin to a guardian with GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS=true + CORS allowlist + a direct principal, exercising probeHealth (incl. the 'blocked' CORS state), sendMessage, and SSE subscribeEvents; today guardian-side (packages/guardian/src/proxy-direct.test.ts, cors.test.ts) and client-side (tests/transport-*.test.ts) are each tested in isolation only.
- [ ] Update the issue/close-out text and docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes.md to reflect the as-built shape (the issue's 'same SvelteKit build, /api/runtime returns pwa-static' predates the ratified two-artifact split — the client-only install is now the @openpalm/client static SPA seeded by runtime-config.json, not a capability-hidden host build), and note that hosted-origin install + pairing UX + HTTPS-for-remote enforcement are tracked in #511/#557, not here.

## Test strategy

Test-first per package, matching each package's existing runner. packages/client uses `bun test` against tests/*.test.ts (run `cd packages/client && bun test`): extend tests/connections-store.test.ts / connections-seed.test.ts for kind persistence if the kind selector is wired, and tests/transport-health.test.ts / transport-health-cors.test.ts patterns for any guardian-/oc-aware URL handling; Playwright e2e lives in e2e/*.pw.ts (`npm run test:e2e`, browsers via `npm run test:browsers` — note plan §12.6 says browser download is proxy-blocked in the dev container, so treat e2e as CI-lane). packages/cli uses `bun test` (tests co-located: src/commands/app.test.ts, src/commands/client-serve.test.ts, src/lib/ui-server.test.ts) — write the failing test first for `openpalm app` on a not-installed OP_HOME serving instead of throwing (ui-server.test.ts already covers ensureValidState/resolveServeState branches with injectable deps). packages/ui uses vitest with *.vitest.ts files (`cd packages/ui && npm run test:unit -- --run`): extend src/lib/server/endpoints-connection-kind.vitest.ts for kind on addConnection, src/lib/resolve-landing.vitest.ts for any landing changes, src/routes/api/connections/server.vitest.ts for API changes. packages/guardian uses `bun test` (src/*.test.ts): proxy-direct.test.ts and cors.test.ts are the reference harnesses for a new direct-principal + CORS end-to-end test; admin.test.ts covers principal minting. Repo-wide check gates: `npm run check` in packages/ui and packages/client (svelte-check --fail-on-warnings) and the client bundle purity test (packages/client/tests/purity.test.ts) must stay green after any client change.

## Dependencies (0.13.0 open issues)

- #511 (PWA/hosted install) — owns the hosted-origin deploy, install affordances, and the pairing/QR connection-setup UX (plan §12.3 items 2-4); #486's 'installable client-only mode' on phones and paste-or-scan pairing complete there, so #486 should scope itself to the localhost/LAN client story and hand the rest to #511.
- #435 (Guardian auth) — the issue's resolved auth decision is 'Guardian Basic auth aligned with #435 Bearer seam'; basicTokenAuthStrategy + the AuthStrategy seam are landed in packages/guardian/src/auth.ts, but any remaining #435 changes to the direct-principal/Bearer surface directly shape the credential a remote client stores, so the provisioning-flow work item should coordinate.
- #557 (Guardian TLS + CORS) — hard prerequisite only for the phone/hosted-HTTPS story; requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections is computed but unenforced (zero consumers), and the refusal UX belongs to #557/Phase 6.5, not #486. LAN plain-HTTP remote connections work today without it.
- #488 (mDNS) — related, non-blocking: LAN discovery would auto-fill the connection URL that /connections currently requires the user to paste; #486 works without it.

## Risks

- Scope creep with #511: pairing/QR, hosted origin, and install affordances are explicitly deferred to #511 in the plan (§12.3) and ui-runtime-modes.md 'Not Yet Shipped' — re-implementing them under #486 would duplicate tracked work.
- Loosening ensureValidState() for `openpalm app` touches the D1/D2/A4 supervisor logic in ui-server.ts that was recently hardened by review fixes (instance-identity probe, client fallback); a careless change can reintroduce the 'attach to wrong hostMode' or orphaned-child failure modes documented inline.
- The issue body describes the pre-split architecture (one SvelteKit build, /api/runtime in client-only mode); implementing it literally would conflict with the ratified two-artifact split — close-out must be against the as-built design, not the issue text.
- Credential provisioning has a real security boundary: direct principals + GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS expose the assistant to the LAN; the I3 posture fix (non-loopback bind without auth → warning + no client co-process) must not be weakened by any new convenience flow.
- Guardian /oc direct-tier connections are silently CORS-denied unless both GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS and GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS are set — the remediation copy exists in the client UI, but a doc-only provisioning flow that forgets either knob produces a confusing 'blocked (CORS)' dead end.
- packages/ui browser-project vitest files and Playwright browser installs are proxy-blocked in dev containers (plan §12.6) — e2e verification of the remote-attach path may only be runnable in CI or a real environment.

## Original issue body

# #486: Remote-only (client) install: connect to a remote assistant/stack

## Summary

Support installing OpenPalm as a **client only** — no local stack — and connecting to an **assistant running on another computer or container**. Also covers the PWA install path (same app, connection-management-only mode).

## Plan

Implemented as part of the UI Runtime Modes refactor. See `docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes-plan.md` for the full design.

### Architecture decisions (resolved)

- **Connection management moves to `/connections`** (new route, no longer under `/admin`). All modes — host, browser, PWA — can reach it without host admin auth.
- **`ConnectionEntry` model** replaces the old endpoint model. Adds a `kind` field (`local-opencode` | `remote-opencode` | `openpalm-client-api`). `endpoints.json` is not renamed.
- **`pwa-static` host mode** is the client-only install. The same SvelteKit build; capabilities hide host controls. No local assistant/guardian containers started. UI is the only process.
- **Auth**: Guardian Basic auth matching the OpenCode implementation. Coordinated with #435 — no parallel credential mechanism.
- **Connection config**: stored in `endpoints.json` under `OP_HOME/config/`. Credentials remain file-based secrets (`knowledge/secrets/`), consistent with the existing secret boundary.
- **Connection status**: surfaced in the `/connections` UI and in the chat empty state.
- **Wizard deep-link**: after a "set up later" install, landing at `/connections/new` is the default when no connection is configured.

### What a client-only install exposes

- `/connections` — add/switch/manage remote assistants
- `/chat` — when an active connection is established
- `/api/runtime` — public, returns `hostMode: 'pwa-static'` and connection-scoped capabilities
- No host lifecycle, no Docker, no `/api/host/*`

### What a remote assistant exposes for clients to attach to

The Guardian `/oc/*` ingress (existing). The `openpalm-client-api` connection kind (preferred for mobile/PWA) routes through Guardian. The `remote-opencode` kind connects to a raw OpenCode instance directly (dev/advanced only).

## Implementation

- **Phase 2** of the runtime modes plan: `routes/connections/`, `/api/connections/*`, internal model rename
- **Phase 6**: PWA manifest + service worker enabling the installable client-only mode

## Open questions (resolved)

- ~~What does a remote stack expose for a client to attach to?~~ → Guardian `/oc/*` ingress
- ~~How is the remote endpoint authenticated?~~ → Guardian Basic auth; aligned with #435 Bearer seam
- ~~Should a client-only install skip seeding assistant/guardian compose services?~~ → Yes. `pwa-static` host mode starts no containers.

## Related

- `docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes-plan.md` — full plan
- #435 — Guardian auth (coordinates the remote auth strategy)
- #433 — Guardian state store (principal registry used by remote connections)
- #488 — mDNS (how remote assistants advertise themselves on LAN)
